missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

The retro-reflective devices shall have the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities, in the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.
For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
The lamps shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except that this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, and the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON, the front or rear position lamp shall fulfill the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions.

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
All categories of vehicles shall be equipped with two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility for S1 or S2 categories devices shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°; (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
While daytime running lamps are not switched ON, the rear position lamp shall have a mandatory closed-circuit tell-tale.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
The lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall have all measurements made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.

The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements for luminous intensity and standard light distribution in Table 4, however, a luminous intensity of 6.0·10¹ cd (60 cd) shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7 for luminous intensity and standard light distribution.
The measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3.
When reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps are operated for 1 minute and for 10 minutes, the luminous intensities shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensities for all other lamps (other than those mentioned in 1.2.1), measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: Markings on the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect the ESA sample and drawings: confirm the markings conform to paragraph 5.3. A marking that is hidden when the lamp is installed in the vehicle is acceptable; pass if the paragraph 5.3 marking is present, regardless of visibility after installation.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions.
extra.test_case: Measure broadband and narrowband radiated emissions per UN R10 Annex 7 and Annex 8 with all lamp functions energised; pass if emissions are below the R10 ESA reference limits.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for conducted emissions.
extra.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions on the supply lines per UN R10 Annex 10 while switching each lamp function; pass if the R10 conducted emission requirements are met.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
extra.test_case: Expose ESA to radiated fields per UN R10 Annex 9 with lamps operating; pass if no degradation of the lamp functions (no unintended switching, flicker or loss of light output) per test plan criteria.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
extra.test_case: Apply conducted transients on supply lines per UN R10 Annex 10 with lamps operating; pass if lamp functions show no malfunction per the specified functional status/pass criteria.

extra.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement, 75 to 400 MHz; pass if measured values are below the limit increasing logarithmically from 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m per Appendix 6.

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission test, 75-400 MHz, all lamp functions operating; pass if measured level below the log-increasing limit 42→53 dBµV/m (Appendix 7).

extra.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 per Annex 10 on 12 V supply; pass if the measured positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +75 V.

extra.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be -100 V.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 per Annex 10 on 12 V supply; pass if the measured negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -100 V in magnitude.

extra.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +150 V.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 per Annex 10 on 24 V supply; pass if the measured positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +150 V.

extra.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be -450 V.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 per Annex 10 on 24 V supply; pass if the measured negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -450 V in magnitude.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 60 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline, 20-400 MHz: apply 60 V/m over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 50 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline, 20-400 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 50 V/m. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the TEM cell method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band shall be 75 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell, 20-200 MHz: apply 75 V/m over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the TEM cell method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band shall be 62,5 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell, 20-200 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 62,5 V/m. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the BCI method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 60 mA.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 BCI, 20-400 MHz: inject 60 mA over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the BCI method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 50 mA.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 BCI, 20-400 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 50 mA. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 30 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 80-2,000 MHz: apply 30 V/m over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 25 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 80-2,000 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 25 V/m. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 10 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 2,000-6,000 MHz: apply 10 V/m over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 8 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE, 2,000-6,000 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 8 V/m. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 21 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, LUF-2,000 MHz: apply 21 V/m over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 18 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, LUF-2,000 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 18 V/m. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 7 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, 2,000-6,000 MHz: apply 7 V/m over >90 % of test frequencies. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 6 V/m.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber, 2,000-6,000 MHz: confirm no frequency is tested below 6 V/m. Pass: no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: Where the rear combination lamp ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8.
extra.test_case: Review the circuit design and component list for any electronic oscillator (e.g. switching LED driver, PWM, microcontroller clock) above 9 kHz. Pass if none is present, so narrowband emission testing under 6.6.2/Annex 8 is waived. Otherwise testing per Annex 8 is required.

extra.text: ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Assess the lamp functions against the immunity related functions criteria. The stop and rear position signalling functions are typically immunity related. Pass for the exemption only if no function is immunity related. Otherwise perform radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 with no disturbance of signalling functions.

extra.text: The radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) in the 30-75 MHz frequency band given by E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30), where F is the frequency in MHz (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).
extra.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions of the lamp ESA per the R10 ESA broadband method (Annex 7) at 120 kHz bandwidth from 30 to 75 MHz with all lamp functions operating; pass if every measured level is at or below 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: The radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) in the 75-400 MHz frequency band given by E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75), where F is the frequency in MHz (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).
extra.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions of the lamp ESA per the R10 ESA broadband method (Annex 7) at 120 kHz bandwidth from 75 to 400 MHz with all lamp functions operating; pass if every measured level is at or below 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m.

extra.text: The radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz frequency band (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).
extra.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions of the lamp ESA per the R10 ESA broadband method (Annex 7) at 120 kHz bandwidth from 400 to 1,000 MHz with all lamp functions operating; pass if every measured level is at or below 63 dBµV/m.

extra.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation) in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Measure ESA narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 method referenced in para 6.6.2.1 with a 120 kHz bandwidth across 30-75 MHz. Pass if every measured value is at or below 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation) in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Measure ESA narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 method referenced in para 6.6.2.1 with a 120 kHz bandwidth across 75-400 MHz. Pass if every measured value is at or below 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m.

extra.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation) in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall be E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Measure ESA narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 method referenced in para 6.6.2.1 with a 120 kHz bandwidth across 400-1,000 MHz. Pass if every measured value is at or below 53 dBµV/m.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 para 2.1; operate all lamp functions in normal mode at maximum load during the emission scan; pass if the operating state is documented and maintained throughout the measurement.

extra.text: As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), an open area test site (OATS) which complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4 may be used for the rear combination lamp ESA test.
extra.test_case: If OATS is used, verify site compliance with CISPR 16-1-4 (Figure 1 of the appendix to Annex 7).

extra.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply to the rear combination lamp ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 scan 30–1,000 MHz in ALSE/OATS; pass if emissions are below the para 6.5 broadband limits throughout the range.

extra.text: If peak detectors are used for measuring the rear combination lamp ESA emissions, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied, the limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. of this Regulation being for quasi-peak detectors.
extra.test_case: Check the test report: peak readings compared with quasi-peak limits plus 20 dB correction per CISPR 12.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the radiated narrowband emission tests.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 para 2: operate the lamp with its functions energised in normal operation, preferably all functions at maximum load; check that the operating state is recorded in the test report.

extra.text: As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), an open area test site (OATS) may be used for the radiated narrowband emission test of the ESA, provided that it complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 para 3.2: if OATS used, verify site validation to CISPR 16-1-4 (Figure 1 of appendix to Annex 7).

extra.text: The narrowband emission limits for the ESA shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Annex 8 para 4.1: scan 30-1,000 MHz; pass if emissions are below the para 6.6.2.1 limits throughout the range.

extra.text: The narrowband emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with an average detector.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 para 4.2: verify average detector setting in test report.

extra.text: Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments may be used for conformity measurements provided that they meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 para 4.3: verify instrument compliance with CISPR 16-1-1.

extra.text: The ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9 being covered: (a) Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) Stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) Reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
extra.test_case: Review test plan: selected ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz; pass if no frequency gap.

extra.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for the immunity tests of the ESA shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check test report references ISO 11452-1 for frequency range and general conditions.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 tests: verify all lamp functions energised in normal operation during exposure.

extra.text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check step size and dwell time in test report against ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: As an alternative the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
extra.test_case: ISO 11451-4 in-vehicle BCI, substitution method, probe at 150 mm from ESA.

extra.text: The immunity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply shall be ensured, and conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited, using the test method of Annex 10.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 method: perform the ISO 7637-2 transient immunity tests, the ISO 16750-2 starting profile test and the ISO 7637-2 transient emission measurement on the supply lines. Pass when immunity and emission meet the applicable criteria.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: circle with letter "E" and country number present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: identification symbols for each approved function (e.g. R, S, AR) present per 3.2.4.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "148R" followed by correct two-digit series of amendments.

extra.text: The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of rear position lamps.
extra.test_case: Check arrow direction on each handed unit against installed orientation; arrow points outwards from vehicle.

extra.text: If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
extra.test_case: If function approved as assembly of two independent lamps: verify "D" to the right of the function symbol.

extra.text: If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
extra.test_case: If function is part of an interdependent lamp system: verify "Y" to the right of the function symbol.

extra.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution, see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
extra.test_case: If approved with reduced light distribution per Annex 3 §1.1: verify vertical downward arrow from horizontal segment.

extra.text: Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with non-replaceable light sources.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: rated voltage (e.g. 12V) or voltage range marked on lamp.

extra.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: If external control gear exists: visual inspection for identification number and manufacturer name.

extra.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, and this marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: If single approval mark used: verify mark visible after installation on vehicle.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: Inspect design: removing any light-transmitting part necessarily removes the approval mark.

extra.text: Each lamp submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Verify by inspection and testing that each lamp function meets all requirements of UN R148 paragraphs 4. and 5. (general specifications, photometry, colour, etc.); pass if all applicable sub-requirements are met.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector).
extra.test_case: Review of the applicable sections 5 and 6 of UN R48 (series of amendments in force at the time of application) and the referenced Annexes; each applicable provision must be checked against the lamp design documentation and samples; pass if all applicable provisions are met.

extra.text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 pertinent to each lamp of the rear combination lamp and to the vehicle category M1 on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: For each lamp function, identify the UN R48 provisions relevant to M1 that are verifiable at lamp level (e.g. geometric visibility, orientation and colour), then verify them by inspection or photometric/goniometric measurement on the lamp sample; pass if all lamp-level verifiable provisions are met.

extra.text: An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to rear position lamps.
extra.test_case: Check the approval documentation and the lamp markings: if the rear position lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", confirm the "D" approval covers only the rear position lamp function. Pass if no "D" marking is applied to a function not listed in 4.4.1, such as the reversing lamp.

extra.text: An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to stop lamps.
extra.test_case: Check the approval documentation and the lamp markings: if the stop lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", confirm the "D" approval covers only the stop lamp function. Pass if no "D" marking is applied to a function not listed in 4.4.1.

extra.text: An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to rear position lamps.
extra.test_case: Check the approval documentation and the lamp markings: if the rear position lamp is an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", confirm the "Y" approval covers only the rear position lamp function. Pass if no "Y" marking is applied to a function not listed in 4.4.2, such as the reversing lamp.

extra.text: An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to stop lamps.
extra.test_case: Check the approval documentation and the lamp markings: if the stop lamp is an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", confirm the "Y" approval covers only the stop lamp function. Pass if no "Y" marking is applied to a function not listed in 4.4.2.

extra.text: Rear position lamps which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, are permitted.
extra.test_case: Design review of circuit/PCB: confirm common light source and permanent intensity-regulation system for the reciprocally incorporated functions; pass if the arrangement matches this description.

extra.text: Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of stop lamp apparent surface; pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of reversing lamp apparent surface; pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: In a single lamp of the rear combination lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review the circuit diagram and LED wiring (series strings) and confirm which LED groups are treated as one light source for the failure assessment. Pass if the grouping used in the failure assessment matches the actual wiring.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case a note in the communication form states that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
extra.test_case: Disable each light source (or LED group) in turn and measure on a goniophotometer at the Annex 3 grid points. Pass if all minimum intensities are still met and the maxima are not exceeded with all sources on. Alternatively, verify that a failure signal for the tell-tale is produced for each single failure and that the communication form carries the corresponding note.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the stop lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.7.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case a note in the communication form states that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
extra.test_case: Disable each light source (or LED group) in turn and carry out photometry at the Annex 3 grid points. Pass if all minimum intensities are still met and the maxima are not exceeded with all sources on. Alternatively, verify that a failure tell-tale signal is generated for each single failure and that the communication form carries the corresponding note.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the reversing lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.4.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case a note in the communication form states that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
extra.test_case: Disable each light source (or LED group) in turn and carry out photometry at the Annex 3 grid points. Pass if all minimum intensities are still met and the maxima are not exceeded with all sources on. Alternatively, verify that a failure tell-tale signal is produced for each single failure and that the communication form carries the corresponding note.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure the luminous intensity. Pass if the steady-intensity requirements of the respective category are fulfilled automatically, without any manual intervention.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and carry out photometry. Pass if the steady-intensity requirements of the respective category are met automatically.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and carry out photometry. Pass if the steady-intensity requirements of the respective category are met automatically.

extra.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
extra.test_case: Attempt swapping modules of different functions/characteristics within the housing, with tools; pass if no swap is possible.

extra.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate the lamp with the control gear under the conditions declared by the applicant; pass if the test conditions match the declaration.

extra.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate the lamp under the conditions declared by the applicant (voltage/current); pass if the test conditions match the declaration.

extra.text: If the applicant requests the additional test to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No.48, the maximum intensity in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1cd, and this additional test may be conducted taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.
extra.test_case: On request, measure the field H 165°–180° outboard, V -2.5° to +5°, optionally with the vehicle body; pass if the maximum is ≤ 0.25 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously at the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure stop+position together and position alone at grid points within ±5° V, ±10° H; pass if the ratio is ≥ 5:1 at each point.

extra.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
extra.test_case: Energise the lamp with its own LED light sources installed, under paragraph 4.8 conditions, and measure the chromaticity. Pass: the colour meets the limits for each function.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd, in accordance with Table 4.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement on both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a); pass if the minimum luminous intensity is at least 4 cd

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) supplied shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp, or 8.5∙10^0 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", except that a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement on both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if intensity ≤ 17 cd (single) or ≤ 8.5 cd (marked "D"), with up to 60 cd allowed below 5° down when reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd, in accordance with Table 4.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement on both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a); pass if the minimum luminous intensity is at least 4 cd

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) supplied shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 4.2∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp, or 2.1∙10^1 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", except that a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement on both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if intensity ≤ 42 cd (single) or ≤ 21 cd (marked "D"), with up to 60 cd allowed below 5° down when reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp supplied shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1, in accordance with Table 4.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of the light distribution grid per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c), Figure A3-I and Table A2-1 on both samples; pass if all grid point requirements are met

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility, in accordance with Table 4.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement within the angles of geometric visibility per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d); pass if intensity ≥ 0.05 cd in all directions

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Verify behaviour under failure conditions per paragraph 4.6; pass if provisions of paragraph 4.6 are met

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples on the reference axis; pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S1 (steady) stop lamp used as a single lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60∙10^2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement over the light distribution of both samples; pass if no value exceeds 260 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S1 (steady) stop lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.30∙10^2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples of a lamp marked D; pass if no value exceeds 130 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at the Table A2-1 grid points on both samples; pass if each point meets its required percentage of the minimum.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10^-1 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement within the Figure A3-I geometric visibility field on both samples; pass if all values ≥ 0.3 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S2 (variable) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples on the reference axis; pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S2 (variable) stop lamp used as a single lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 7.30∙10^2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples in the highest intensity condition; pass if no value exceeds 730 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S2 (variable) stop lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.65∙10^2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples of a lamp marked D; pass if no value exceeds 365 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S2 (variable) stop lamp shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at the Table A2-1 grid points on both samples; pass if each point meets its required percentage.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S2 (variable) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10^-1 cd (day) within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement in day mode within the Figure A3-I field on both samples; pass if all values ≥ 0.3 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of a category S2 (variable) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 7∙10^-2 cd (night) within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement in night mode within the Figure A3-I field on both samples; pass if all values ≥ 0.07 cd.

extra.text: The stop lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Verify failure behaviour per paragraph 4.6 (e.g. simulated LED failure); pass if paragraph 4.6 provisions are met.

extra.text: The minimum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on the reference axis per para 4.8.3.1.(a); pass if ≥ 80 cd.

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR in or above the h-plane shall be 3.00∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of all directions in or above the H-plane per para 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if ≤ 300 cd.

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR below the h-plane, down to 5°D, shall be 6.00∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan between H-plane and 5°D; pass if ≤ 600 cd.

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR below 5°D shall be 8.00∙10^3 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan below 5°D; pass if ≤ 8000 cd.

extra.text: The standard light distribution of the reversing lamp of category AR shall be as defined in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at grid points of Figure A3-V per para 4.8.3.1.(c); pass if each point meets its percentage of the minimum.

extra.text: In the case where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at 30° inwards; pass if ≥ 25 cd.

extra.text: The failure provisions of paragraph 4.6 shall apply to the reversing lamp.
extra.test_case: Verify failure behaviour per paragraph 4.6 with simulated LED failures; pass if paragraph 4.6 criteria are met.

extra.text: For the required minimum value of 7∙10-1 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to 5∙10-1 cd (equivalent 20 per cent) and 3∙10-1 cd (equivalent 30 per cent) as shown in Table 12.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if values are not below 5∙10-1 cd (20 per cent level) / 3∙10-1 cd (30 per cent level).

extra.text: For the required minimum value of 6∙10-1 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to 4∙10-1 cd (equivalent 20 per cent) and 2∙10-1 cd (equivalent 30 per cent) as shown in Table 12.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if values are not below 4∙10-1 cd (20 per cent level) / 2∙10-1 cd (30 per cent level).

extra.text: For the required minimum value of 3∙10-1 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to 2∙10-1 cd (equivalent 20 per cent) and 1∙10-1 cd (equivalent 30 per cent) as shown in Table 12.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if values are not below 2∙10-1 cd (20 per cent level) / 1∙10-1 cd (30 per cent level).

extra.text: For the required minimum value of 7∙10-2 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to 5∙10-2 cd (equivalent 20 per cent) and 3∙10-2 cd (equivalent 30 per cent) as shown in Table 12.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if values are not below 5∙10-2 cd (20 per cent level) / 3∙10-2 cd (30 per cent level).

extra.text: For the required minimum value of 5∙10-2 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to 3∙10-2 cd (equivalent 20 per cent) and 2∙10-2 cd (equivalent 30 per cent) as shown in Table 12.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if values are not below 3∙10-2 cd (20 per cent level) / 2∙10-2 cd (30 per cent level).

extra.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of 45° inboard / 80° outboard.
extra.test_case: Goniometric check of the lamp against Annex 2, Part A, Table A2-1 (right-side unit; mirrored for the left). Pass if the light-emitting surface is visible at 45° inboard and 80° outboard.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard below the H-plane, the reduced angles being used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
extra.test_case: Confirm the mounting height of the H-plane on the M1 vehicle is below 750 mm, then verify visibility below the H-plane per Table A2-1 note a. Pass if visible at 20° inboard and 80° outboard.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below.
extra.test_case: Goniometric check per Annex 2, Table A2-1. Pass if the lamp is visible at 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.

extra.text: For rear position lamps (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be 15° above / 5° below.
extra.test_case: Check the installed H-plane height is below 750 mm, then perform a goniometric check per Table A2-1 note b. Pass if the lamp is visible at 15° above and 5° below.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of the stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of 45° inboard / 45° outboard.
extra.test_case: Goniometric check per Annex 2, Part A, Table A2-1. Pass if the lamp is visible at 45° inboard and 45° outboard.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of the stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard below the H-plane, the reduced angles being used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
extra.test_case: Confirm the installed H-plane height is below 750 mm, then verify visibility below the H-plane per Table A2-1 note a. Pass if visible at 20° inboard and 45° outboard.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of the stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below.
extra.test_case: Goniometric check per Annex 2, Table A2-1. Pass if the lamp is visible at 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.

extra.text: For stop lamps (S1, S2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be 15° above / 5° below.
extra.test_case: Check the installed H-plane height is below 750 mm, then perform a goniometric check per Table A2-1 note b. Pass if the lamp is visible at 15° above and 5° below.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of a rear position lamp pair (MR) shall have minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15° above / 5° below for lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).
extra.test_case: If the lamp is approved as MR, perform a goniometric check per Table A2-1. Pass if all the stated angles are met for the installed mounting height.

extra.text: The geometric visibility of a stop lamp pair (MS) shall have minimum horizontal angles of 0° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15° above / 5° below for lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).
extra.test_case: If the lamp is approved as MS, perform a goniometric check per Table A2-1. Pass if all the stated angles are met for the installed mounting height.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement of the rear position lamp and stop lamp, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Photometric goniometer measurement relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°) through the centre of reference; compute the required minimum per direction as the percentage of the required minimum, rounded down to three significant digits. Pass if every measured value is at least that value.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the manufacturer-declared mounting height. If it is ≤ 750 mm, perform photometric verification of the downward directions only to 5° down. Pass if all points within the reduced field meet the minima.

extra.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the manufacturer-declared mounting height and the stop lamp category. If it is ≤ 750 mm, verify photometry downward only to 5° down. Pass if all points within the reduced field meet the minima.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, where the values shown give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).
extra.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at all Figure A3-I points. Pass if each point is at least the stated percentage of the required minimum for the rear position lamp from the applicable table.

extra.text: The stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, where the values shown give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 7).
extra.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at all Figure A3-I points. Pass if each point is at least the stated percentage of the Table 7 minimum for the stop lamp category.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V, where the values shown give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities in cd, the directions H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the axis of reference and passing through the centre of reference.
extra.test_case: Align the reversing lamp to the axis of reference through the centre of reference. Measure intensity at each Figure A3-V point. Pass if each value is ≥ the cd value shown.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the rear combination lamp shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement under paragraph 4.9 conditions; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed boundaries.

extra.text: In any test of conformity carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used with the consent of the competent authority responsible for approval tests, provided the manufacturer proves that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Check for authority consent and equivalence evidence for any alternative method.

extra.text: From a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, the differences of the mass-produced rear combination lamp from the requirements of this Regulation shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
extra.test_case: Dimensional and mechanical inspection of randomly sampled production lamps against the approved drawings; pass if deviations are within inevitable manufacturing tolerances.

extra.text: With respect to photometric performance, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any rear combination lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Photometric test per paragraph 4.8. on randomly chosen production lamps; pass if no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the rear combination lamp shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.; pass if chromaticity coordinates are within the prescribed colour boundaries.

extra.text: For reversing lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.1: operate reversing lamp, measure intensity distribution after 1 min and after 10 min (or calculate from distribution after photometric stability using HV ratios at 1 min, 10 min and stability); pass if all test points are within min/max limits.

extra.text: The luminous intensity distribution of the reversing lamp after 1 and after 10 minutes of operation may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured after photometric stability has occurred by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV: (a) After 1 minute; (b) After 10 minutes; and (c) After photometric stability has occurred.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity at 1 min, 10 min and at photometric stability; scale the stabilised distribution by the HV ratios; pass if calculated values at all test points meet min/max requirements.

extra.text: For the rear position lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2: measure intensity distribution after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability); pass if all test points are within min/max limits.

extra.text: For the stop lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2: measure intensity distribution after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability); pass if all test points are within min/max limits.

extra.text: The luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp after 1 min of operation may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution either after 30 min of operation or after photometric stabilization, by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 min and either after 30 min of operation or after photometric stabilization.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity after 1 min and after 30 min or at stabilisation; scale distribution by HV ratio; pass if calculated 1 min values meet min/max requirements at all test points.

extra.text: The luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as the reference coordinate.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity at 4 s after switch-on (or derive distribution via HV ratio from para 1 measurement); pass if min/max requirements met, or deemed compliant for LED-only per para 2.1.2.

extra.text: The luminous intensity distribution of the stop lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as the reference coordinate.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity at 0.2 s after switch-on (or derive distribution via HV ratio); pass if min/max requirements met, or deemed compliant for LED-only per para 2.1.2.

extra.text: The luminous intensity distribution of the reversing lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as the reference coordinate.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity at 0.2 s after switch-on (or derive distribution via HV ratio); pass if min/max requirements met, or deemed compliant for LED-only per para 2.1.2.

extra.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be as defined in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Measure the approval marking dimensions and compare with the value of "a" in Table 1 (arrangement per Annex 10 examples). Pass: dimensions meet Table 1.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the marking. Pass: circled "E" with the distinguishing number of the approving country is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: identification symbol (e.g. class IA) per paragraph 3.2.5 is present in the marking.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "150R" followed by the two-digit series of amendments in force at approval is present.

extra.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Review manufacturer's prescribed rotation angles; if orientation is ambiguous, visually check "TOP" is inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Install the lamp on the vehicle or representative fixture and verify visually that the single approval mark/UI is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check: each removable light-transmitting part (outer lens, reversing insert) cannot be removed without also removing the approval mark/UI.

extra.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Production samples tested against R150 paragraphs 4 and 5 requirements (photometric, colorimetric, physical); pass if samples conform to approved type.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications", and in the Annexes referenced in those sections, of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval shall apply to the retro-reflector.
extra.test_case: Review the applicable UN R48 series of amendments in force at the time of application. Check the retro-reflector against R48 sections 5 and 6 and the referenced Annexes (e.g. 6.14 rear retro-reflector, non-triangular), including position, geometric visibility, orientation and colour. Pass if all requirements that can be verified at device approval are met.

extra.text: The requirements pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Identify the R48 requirements relevant to a rear non-triangular retro-reflector on M1 vehicles that can be verified at device level. Verify them by document review and measurement on the device as mounted per the applicant's installation drawing. Pass if all feasible requirements are verified and met.

extra.text: For testing the daytime colour of the retro-reflective device, the material shall be illuminated by the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664- 2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a) as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Measure the daytime colour of the retro-reflector material under the CIE D65 illuminant, using (45a:0) or (0:45a) geometry per Annex 4, Part 2. Pass: the test is performed under these conditions and the result is recorded for comparison with the applicable daytime colour limits.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in the paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2 (visual, trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) after each group's tests; pass if within red night-time limits of UN R48.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value for a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB must be equal to or greater than 3.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value for a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB must be equal to or greater than 2.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angles β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry at α = 20', β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 200 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value for a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB must be equal to or greater than 1.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angles β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
extra.test_case: Photometry at α = 20', β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°; pass if RI ≥ 100 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value for a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB must be equal to or greater than 5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 at an angle of divergence of 1°30' and illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry at α = 1°30', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 5 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value for a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB must be equal to or greater than 2.8∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 at an angle of divergence of 1°30' and illumination angles β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry at α = 1°30', β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 2.8 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value for a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB must be equal to or greater than 2.5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 at an angle of divergence of 1°30' and illumination angles β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
extra.test_case: Photometry at α = 1°30', β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°; pass if RI ≥ 2.5 mcd/lx.
